canada/stanley-park.name: Stanley Park seawall
canada/stanley-park.description: A forested peninsula ringed by a flat seawall path, with totem poles and city views.
canada/stanley-park.details: Stanley Park covers over 400 hectares at the edge of downtown Vancouver. The 9-kilometre seawall is walked or cycled, passing Brockton Point totem poles, beaches and the Lions Gate Bridge. Bike rentals are plentiful nearby. Allow half a day.

canada/granville-island.name: Granville Island Public Market
canada/granville-island.description: A food market and arts district under a bridge, reached by small ferry.
canada/granville-island.details: Granville Island has the Public Market with produce, smoked salmon and bakeries, plus studios, theatres and a brewery. Aqua-Bus ferries cross False Creek. It is busy at weekends, so go on a weekday morning.

canada/capilano.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge and Grouse Mountain
canada/capilano.description: Forest walks and cable-car views on the North Shore mountains.
canada/capilano.details: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park has a 137-metre swaying bridge over a canyon, with treetop walkways in a rainforest. Grouse Mountain has a gondola for city views and, in winter, skiing and snowshoeing. Both are 20 to 30 minutes north of downtown.

canada/banff-gondola.name: Banff town and Sulphur Mountain Gondola
canada/banff-gondola.description: A mountain town with a gondola to a ridge-top boardwalk and hot springs nearby.
canada/banff-gondola.details: Banff is a lively town in the Rockies, with shops, restaurants and a view of Cascade Mountain. The gondola rises to the Sulphur Mountain summit with a boardwalk and a panorama. The Upper Hot Springs are close. The area is in Banff National Park, and a park pass is needed.

canada/lake-louise-moraine.name: Lake Louise and Moraine Lake
canada/lake-louise-moraine.description: The two most famous turquoise lakes in the Canadian Rockies.
canada/lake-louise-moraine.details: Lake Louise sits beneath a glacier and has a shoreline walk and the grand lodge. Moraine Lake lies in the Valley of the Ten Peaks. Access to Moraine Lake is by shuttle or tour only in summer, so reserve ahead. Arrive early for parking, and expect snow into early summer.

canada/johnston-canyon.name: Johnston Canyon
canada/johnston-canyon.description: A catwalk trail up a limestone canyon to waterfalls.
canada/johnston-canyon.details: A well-built walkway is attached to the canyon walls and leads to the Lower Falls in about 20 minutes and the Upper Falls after 45 minutes. In winter people join guided ice walks. It is busy in summer, so start early.

canada/icefields-parkway.name: Icefields Parkway and Columbia Icefield
canada/icefields-parkway.description: One of the most scenic drives in the world, with glaciers, lakes and wildlife viewing.
canada/icefields-parkway.details: The Icefields Parkway links Lake Louise and Jasper over 230 kilometres, passing Peyto Lake, Bow Lake and Athabasca Falls. At the Columbia Icefield, special buses drive onto the Athabasca Glacier, and a glass-floored skywalk looks into the valley. Allow a full day with stops. Services are limited, so fill up with fuel.

canada/maligne-lake.name: Maligne Lake and Spirit Island
canada/maligne-lake.description: A long mountain lake near Jasper, visited by boat cruise to a tiny island.
canada/maligne-lake.details: Maligne Lake is the largest in the Rockies. A 90-minute cruise reaches Spirit Island, one of the most photographed spots in Canada. The road passes Maligne Canyon and wildlife is often seen along the way. Cruises run from about May to October.

canada/jasper-wildlife.name: Jasper town and wildlife
canada/jasper-wildlife.description: A relaxed mountain town with elk in the streets and hot springs, gondola and dark skies.
canada/jasper-wildlife.details: Jasper is quieter than Banff and in a dark-sky preserve. The SkyTram gives views of six mountain ranges, and the Miette hot springs are a short drive. Wildlife such as elk, bighorn sheep and bears is common, so keep a safe distance and carry bear spray when hiking.

canada/cn-tower.name: CN Tower and Toronto waterfront
canada/cn-tower.description: The 553-metre tower with an EdgeWalk and a glass floor, over the harbour.
canada/cn-tower.details: The CN Tower is a Toronto landmark with an observation deck and a revolving restaurant, and a thrilling outdoor EdgeWalk. The waterfront has the ferry to the Toronto Islands, Harbourfront and the Ripley aquarium. Book timed entry for sunset.

canada/st-lawrence-market.name: St Lawrence Market and Distillery District
canada/st-lawrence-market.description: A historic food hall and a pedestrian neighbourhood of Victorian industrial buildings.
canada/st-lawrence-market.details: St Lawrence Market has stalls of cheese, seafood and the famous peameal bacon sandwich. The Distillery District has cobbled streets, galleries and cafes. Both are good for a relaxed afternoon, and the market is closed on Mondays.

canada/niagara-falls.name: Niagara Falls boat tour
canada/niagara-falls.description: A boat ride to the foot of the Horseshoe Falls, with a view from the Canadian side.
canada/niagara-falls.details: The Hornblower boat takes visitors up close to the base of the Horseshoe Falls, with ponchos given out. The Canadian side has the best views, and the town is touristy. Niagara-on-the-Lake nearby has wineries and a pretty main street. Allow a full day from Toronto.

canada/old-montreal.name: Old Montreal and Notre-Dame Basilica
canada/old-montreal.description: Cobbled streets, a grand basilica and the old port in a French-speaking city.
canada/old-montreal.details: Vieux-Montreal has stone buildings, galleries and restaurants, and the Notre-Dame Basilica has a spectacular blue-and-gold interior. The Old Port has a promenade and a ferris wheel. The city is French first, and a few words of French are appreciated.

canada/mount-royal-jean-talon.name: Mount Royal and Jean-Talon Market
canada/mount-royal-jean-talon.description: A park hill with city views and a big market of produce and Quebec cheese.
canada/mount-royal-jean-talon.details: Mount Royal is the park in the middle of Montreal with a lookout over downtown, easy to walk up. Jean-Talon Market is a lively market in Little Italy with fruit, cheese, maple products and food stalls. Try a bagel and poutine along the way.

canada/quebec-city.name: Old Quebec and Chateau Frontenac
canada/quebec-city.description: The only walled city north of Mexico, with a fairytale hotel above the St Lawrence.
canada/quebec-city.details: Old Quebec is a UNESCO site with cobbled lanes, ramparts and the Chateau Frontenac overlooking the river. The Dufferin Terrace gives views, and Petit-Champlain is the shopping quarter. Montmorency Falls is just outside the city. The funicular links upper and lower town.
